subject: Cognitive Science
title: Neurotransmitters of Attention
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Neurotransmitters of Attention.

hook.text: Three chemicals control your attention: dopamine for goals, norepinephrine for alertness, acetylcholine for focus.

buildup.text: Dopamine from the midbrain fuels executive attention. Low dopamine means poor goal-directed control.

discovery.text: Norepinephrine from the locus coeruleus sets alertness. Too little, you're drowsy. Too much, you're anxious.

twist.text: Acetylcholine sharpens the signal-to-noise ratio. It's why nicotine temporarily boosts focus.

climax.text: ADHD medications work by adjusting dopamine and norepinephrine—not by adding focus, but by tuning chemistry.

punchline.text: Attention runs on chemistry, not willpower.

details.summary: Attention depends on a balance of neurotransmitters including dopamine for motivation and executive control, norepinephrine for alertness, and acetylcholine for orienting to stimuli. Disruptions in these systems underlie attention disorders and explain how caffeine and medications work.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding the chemistry of attention explains why stimulant medications help ADHD, why caffeine sharpens focus, and why stress and sleep deprivation impair concentration.
takeaways: Dopamine supports motivation and executive attention control
Norepinephrine maintains alertness and arousal levels
Acetylcholine enables orienting to relevant stimuli

faq.question: How do ADHD medications work on attention?
faq.answer: Stimulant medications like methylphenidate and amphetamines increase dopamine and norepinephrine levels in the prefrontal cortex. This boosts executive control and alertness, helping individuals sustain focus and resist distractions. The effect is specific to prefrontal circuits.

faq.question: Why does caffeine improve attention?
faq.answer: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors that promote drowsiness, indirectly increasing norepinephrine and dopamine activity. This raises alertness and reduces the feeling of fatigue. It does not create new attentional capacity but prevents the decline caused by tiredness.
